# ignore_rules.rs: each scenario test fails on main and on a mutant of this fix. The r3 rewind rows (works 5, 6 and 7) are the only guard for a file moved out of a displaced folder to an included path, because the engine sync oracle and the battery leave such a copy out until GUN-1341 lands. The restore row checks that both devices hold the write at the same name.
# Engine and store: the miss_local unit test, the merged displaced-write harness test, and the displaced_local_nodes migration test and upgrade case each fail on their own mutant. No existing test covers the displaced map's new state, or #910's found place kept through the recorded_nodes rebuild.
# The release fixture verifies complete chunk backfill, a mismatched key, and an incomplete chunk list. The matching file must send its original chunks as a create.
# The engine and driver tests cover rewind on both sides of displacement and require the file to keep its identity and chunks. The create-in-flight and store reopen cases distinguish an expired record from a confirmed one and check that an identity update keeps the outstanding record.
# The world test verifies the edited bytes and original file identity at an ignored path after another entry takes its old name. The CI seed covers the other simulator's disk model.
# The restart test proves that the prior displaced parent changes the planner's decision after two store reopens. The readmission test distinguishes a proven match from a legacy row, another volume, a reused inode and a stale observation. The disk test keeps the row across a rename and one unlink, then checks its removal in the store after the last unlink. The alpha6 case verifies that the upgrade invents no copy proof.
# Reidentification runs the same overwrite scenario with missing volume proof and live rules. It also checks an unrelated save by rename and that the observer waits for the driver to accept a replacement identity.
# The link tests distinguish a verified alias from single-link proof and keep the displaced record when the alias is already attached to a different node.
# The review regressions test displaced moves, folder relisting, orphan cleanup, edit ancestry and acknowledged content. They also exercise deferred reads, content-free renames, replacement proof, paginated history, and the old in-flight Create upgrade. The store test checks that writing readmission state before its local row fails instead of silently losing it.
# The lost-write check counts a write in an ignored folder inside a parked folder, which the disk still holds, as the engine sync device's own disk check does, while the rules still leave its path out. The battery seed 51ff6ece fails without it.
# The readmission removal test plans a RemoveFile for a file with a waiting position below a displaced folder and requires the completion check to accept it. It fails before this fix and on a mutant that drops the displaced-folder case from that check.
# ignore_rules.rs, rewind rows for a node moved out of a displaced folder: the Publish and Discard tables (folder or file, edit before or after the rewind, with and without a restart), the included-folder contrast and the subfolder repro each fail on main or on a mutant of one clause (the hold, the Discard release, the kept question, the trash). The test for a file deleted here that the rules leave out through a rewind fails when recovery stops asking about excluded nodes with no local copy. The displaced_local_nodes upgrade row at a temp name fails if the migration runs before born_as_temp.
# Readmission rows for a node discarded after a rewind (file or folder, the excluded folder renamed or the rules changed, with and without a restart), the test for a write made after a Discard answer, the reload test for a temp-name file that is displaced or missed, and the device-table harness that runs until no question is left each fail on main or on a mutant of their fix. The simulator change accepts the copy a CreatedAfterRestorePoint Keep makes.
